classification_rationale: Required doc update for a shipped behavior change.

trigger: A future RotationConfirmState enumerator added without a matching switch arm
summary: Switch over RotationConfirmState was exhaustive today but not pragma-guarded like this codebase's own consume_denial_reason idiom, so a future missing arm would warn-only on GCC and be silent on MSVC.
classification_rationale: Codebase has an established idiom for this hazard that was not followed.

trigger: Windows CI runner (Wee Tam) Defender path-exclusion wildcard match on temp DB files
summary: Two new TempDbFile prefixes used hyphenated 'mcp-' style instead of the yuzu_test_ underscore convention needed for the Defender exclusion wildcard.
classification_rationale: Codebase test-convention violation (CLAUDE.md test-helpers section).

trigger: Active-credential set reads empty (kNoneActive) between an approval ticket's mint and its recall - either a genuine revoke-to-zero, or a masked store-read failure
summary: kNoneActive passed through unconditionally, burning the one-time ticket on a no-op; the changelog's 'revoked... denies WITHOUT consuming' claim did not universally hold. Independently found by architect and quality-engineer in the same Gate 3 wave (before either had seen the other's finding); echoed downstream (with added context) by unhappy-path, consistency-auditor, and compliance-officer once the finding was fed into their prompts as context - those are not counted as additional independent reporters.
classification_rationale: Changelog asserted a universal claim the code did not implement; corrected by making the code match the claim.

trigger: A future regression flips the precondition's allow branch to deny-everything
summary: No test proved the precondition's ALLOW path (undrifted recall) reaches the handler and succeeds end-to-end; every existing test exercised only denial or bypassed approval. Reporter's own self-label was BLOCKING; derived band is MEDIUM (a coverage gap with bounded blast radius, not an active defect) - reporter's own vocabulary recorded, derived band governs the gate per CLAUDE.md standing rule 2.
classification_rationale: Missing regression coverage for a real code path.

trigger: A fully black-holed (packet-drop, no RST) TCP path to Postgres during the precondition's list_active_for_principal read
summary: Worst-case worker-pin duration under a black-holed connection is bounded only by OS-default TCP keepalive probe timing (~11.5 min per Gate 6 sre's correction of this finding's own original ~40s estimate), not statement_timeout. Chaos-scenario evidence (CH-4) tracked as #2947, corrected there post-session.
classification_rationale: A real, bounded-but-large availability risk on a shared thread pool.

trigger: A client retries a precondition-denied recall repeatedly during a degraded Postgres period
summary: Retry-storm compounding during a degraded read period; capacity characterization only, no correctness assertion. Folded into #2947's scope (CH-5, depends on CH-4's harness).
classification_rationale: Informational load characterization.

summary: Silent success perceived as failure in one narrow client-retry framing; informational, no action needed.
classification_rationale: Informational.

summary: TOCTOU window widened by the unlocked precondition read but not broken - the CAS and confirm_rotation's own in-transaction recheck remain authoritative.
classification_rationale: Confirmed-safe, informational.

trigger: list_active_for_principal's pool-lease-timeout or query-failure branch fires persistently for one principal
summary: Both silent-return branches produced zero log lines and no metric - a persistent fault for one principal was invisible to on-call. Reinforced with more precision (exact line, exact fix) by sre at Gate 6 once fed as context; not counted as a second independent reporter.
classification_rationale: No observability for a real failure mode.

summary: Confirmed safe: the read-primary in-txn invariant documented in rotation_confirm_state.hpp holds as written.
classification_rationale: Confirmed-safe, informational.

trigger: Two independently-approved tickets pinned to the same successor token_id, recalled concurrently
summary: Both preconditions pass and CAS-consume (different rows); only one confirm_rotation call wins the advisory lock, so the loser's ticket is already burned before its own confirm fails. Known and accepted (an operator double-approval mistake, not an attack); disclosed in code comment and changelog. Deterministic regression test (CH-7, chaos-injector's design) needs a test-only race hook between CAS-consume and lock-acquire - deferred as #2952 rather than added inline, since the hook itself needs its own cpp-safety scrutiny.
classification_rationale: Real, disclosed residual; not silently omitted.

summary: Persistent lockout scenario is self-limiting (bounded by the approval's own TTL); informational.
classification_rationale: Confirmed-safe, informational.

trigger: A future change to confirm_rotation's inline linkage/pin check or to pair_matches_pin only updates one side
summary: pair_matches_pin duplicates confirm_rotation's inline linkage+pin check with no shared symbol forcing sync. A direct swap-in was investigated and rejected (advisor caught it): the inline check reports two DIFFERENT client-visible error classes (retryable vs terminal) that pair_matches_pin's single bool would silently collapse - a correctness regression, not a refactor. Cross-reference comments added at both sites as the cheap mitigation; the actual fix (a reason-enum redesign) deferred as #2953.
classification_rationale: Real drift risk; direct fix would have been a regression.

summary: Audit suffix grammar inconsistency (unenforced), does not co-occur today - informational.
classification_rationale: Informational, unenforced today.

trigger: An operator scans the audit log for a kPrecondition denial
summary: Suggested appending '(ticket not consumed)' to the audit detail suffix for readability without a second query.
classification_rationale: Cheap readability improvement.

trigger: A first-time pilot operator hits a kPrecondition denial and has to guess which tool tells them current rotation state
summary: Remediation text told the operator to check current state but never named a diagnostic tool - plausible support-ticket generator. Reporter's own exposure citation (E2) recorded as disagreeing with this ledger's independent derivation (E3, ordinary operation by any RBAC'd operator, no privilege escalation involved) - both derive MEDIUM regardless, so the gate outcome is unaffected by the disagreement.
classification_rationale: UX gap on a legitimate, expected drift path.

trigger: An operator or agentic worker reads confirm_engine_rotation's tools/list description to learn its denial behavior
summary: tools/list description stated only the pre-existing 'replay of consumed ticket' denial shape, silent on the new first-recall-of-never-consumed-ticket case this PR adds. Truth finding per CLAUDE.md standing rule 3 (domain agent owns truth for in-code description text).
classification_rationale: In-code description contradicted the new shipped behavior.

summary: Optional vNEXT caveat entry mirroring the #2404 precedent format; not mandatory. Declined - marginal value for this PR's scope.
classification_rationale: Optional enhancement, explicitly not required by the reporter.

trigger: An operator wants to distinguish precondition-caused refusals from other refusal kinds in aggregate rate
summary: Recommended a reason label on yuzu_mcp_approval_refused_total. Rejected as specified (advisor caught it): a label on the SHARED counter would reopen the anti-oracle problem for kForeignOrigin vs kNotConsumable, which must stay mutually indistinguishable. Implemented instead as a new DEDICATED counter (yuzu_mcp_approval_precondition_denied_total), safe because kPrecondition is already distinguishable to the client from the response body, unlike the pair the shared counter protects.
classification_rationale: Real observability gap; the specific mechanism proposed would have regressed a security property.

trigger: A black-holed Postgres connection pins an httplib worker for up to ~11.5 minutes (see UP-1/#2947)
summary: Recommended generalizing keepalives_interval/keepalives_count/tcp_user_timeout hardening in connect_one(), ahead of #2939's sweep adding more precondition callers onto the same shared pool. Out of scope for this per-caller PR (affects every PgPool consumer, a broader infra change); not filed as a separate issue - folded into #2947's discussion via comment, where CH-4's worst-case math already lives, rather than creating a third place this risk is described.
classification_rationale: Real, pre-existing gap in shared infra; correctly scoped out of a single-caller PR.

trigger: An assertion throws between sqlite3_open and sqlite3_close in one of the two new TEST_CASEs
summary: Manual sqlite3_open/close in new test code, byte-matching an existing sibling-test pattern already in scope at the original Gate 2 PASS - not a new pattern. Routed to cpp-safety's re-review, which confirmed no policy-floor shape (test-only, not production).
classification_rationale: Pre-existing pattern, not introduced by this diff.

trigger: A future refactor accidentally forwards the specific RotationConfirmState fact to the MCP client
summary: The anti-oracle property (specific fact stays server-side/audit-only) was correct today but had no regression pin. Added a negative CHECK that the specific fact never appears in the client-facing response body.
classification_rationale: Missing regression coverage for a security-relevant property.

trigger: An operator greps the audit log for the doc's quoted example string
summary: Quoted example audit string ('rotation already confirmed') did not match any real emission (the actual kSoleConfirmed message is 'rotation already confirmed; nothing to confirm').
classification_rationale: Doc example string did not match the code producing it.

classification_rationale: Wording-only overclaim of certainty, not a code/doc mismatch.

policy_floor: manual resource cleanup in NEW C++ that is not RAII-wrapped
trigger: Any failing Catch2 REQUIRE between sqlite3_open and sqlite3_close in any of the four new TEST_CASEs (9+ fatal REQUIREs in the first case alone)
summary: CORRECTS SEC-F1 (pass 2, reporter security-guardian): that row's provenance='pre_existing' and disposition='no_change_needed' were wrong. The four sqlite3_open/close pairs are lines this diff ADDS - they resemble ~20 pre-existing sibling sites elsewhere in the same file, but resembling an existing pattern is not the same fact as being pre-existing cleanup in a touched file, which is what SKILL.md's carve-out (line 299) actually requires to avoid the floor. Gate 8's security-guardian sub-review and this run's own ledger-authoring both made that substitution and cleared a genuine floor on self-granted authority - exactly what the 'documented impossibility exception is NOT self-granted' clause (SKILL.md line 297) exists to prevent. Fixed: all four sites wrapped in yuzu::test::SqliteHandleOwner<sqlite3> (tests/unit/test_helpers.hpp:1213), the RAII owner already used at test_authz_topology_floor.cpp:432 for the identical hazard.
classification_rationale: A resource-ownership defect in new test code, misclassified as pre-existing by two prior review passes.

trigger: engine_credential_store_ is null or closed (is_open()==false) when the confirm_engine_rotation precondition runs
summary: NOT caught by any Gate 2-8 agent in passes 1-2 - a genuinely new finding, independent_reporters=1. The precondition's own closed-store branch passed through unconditionally on the stated reasoning that 'the handler's own store-open guard reports this' - but the handler's guard (line ~9118, right before its confirm_rotation call at 9143) runs AFTER consume_ticket (~3529), not before, so the pass-through consumed the ticket first and only then hit the handler's guard: the exact same burn-on-no-op shape as ARCH-1's kNoneActive finding (pass 1), on a different trigger. The fix's own kNoneActive comment block ('deny, don't guess... costs nothing... strictly safer') applies verbatim and was simply not extended to this sibling branch. Fixed: now denies with 'engine credential store unavailable; retry', matching the handler's own transient/retryable framing. New regression test added and mutation-verified (reverted, confirmed the ticket was genuinely consumed under the mutation, restored, confirmed green).
classification_rationale: Same defect CLASS as ARCH-1 (pass 1), on a sibling code path the original fix did not cover - the 'fix ships the next instance of the class it closed' pattern this session's own standing feedback names.

waiver_rationale: Operator (Dave) weighed the cost: folding this in triggers a new governance round and a new external-reviewer pass for a wording-only completeness gap with no BLOCKING/HIGH shape. Left unfixed by explicit decision, not an oversight.
trigger: A reader of the eventual assembled CHANGELOG.md entry for #2443 looks for the full set of denial-without-consume causes
summary: The changelog fragment's 'denies WITHOUT consuming' list (confirmed, revoked, anomalous count, pin mismatch, empty-read) does not mention the closed/unwired-store cause this commit (6f7faf466) also fixed. Not a code/doc contradiction (nothing false is claimed, just incomplete) and this feature is entirely unreleased on this branch, so it is a completeness gap in what will ship, not a breaking-change concealment.
classification_rationale: A real but non-load-bearing completeness gap; the feature's core claim (deny-without-consume) is not contradicted, only under-enumerated.

waiver_rationale: Operator weighed the cost: this is a test-hardening suggestion pinning a property that already holds and is already covered generically by the kNoneActive sibling test's pin on the SAME shared client-response sink - a special-case regression on this specific arm would already be caught there for the general shape. Left unfixed by explicit decision.
trigger: A future code change special-cases the closed-store arm of kPrecondition and routes store-specific detail into the client-facing envelope, bypassing the currently-generic branch
summary: The new closed-store regression test asserts non-consumption and the audit trail but has no negative CHECK pinning that 'engine credential store unavailable' never reaches the client-facing response body - the kNoneActive sibling test already has this exact pin (line ~2062) for its own specific fact. Independently found by security-guardian (F2) and quality-engineer in the same Gate 8 round-2 wave, before either saw the other's output - genuinely 2 independent reporters, same one-line suggested fix from both.
classification_rationale: A real regression-pin gap on an anti-oracle property that holds today but is unpinned; not a live leak (verified: today's code is generic for this arm too).

trigger: Reviewer initially flagged the store-null vs store-not-open operands of the guarding `if` as separately testable
summary: On direct re-read, both operands of `!engine_credential_store_ || !engine_credential_store_->is_open()` short-circuit to the SAME single return statement - there is no code divergence between the two conditions to under-test. Self-resolved as a non-finding during the same review; recorded for completeness.
classification_rationale: Confirmed non-issue on inspection - no actionable defect exists.
